label: PYQ-style
stem: The charge needed to reduce 1 mol of $\ce{MnO4-}$ to $\ce{Mn^2+}$ is
options: 1 F
3 F
5 F
7 F
model_answer: **(c) 5 F.** Mn goes from +7 to +2: $\ce{MnO4- + 8H+ + 5e- -> Mn^2+ + 4H2O}$.

label: PYQ-style
stem: When an electrolyte solution is diluted,
options: $\kappa$ and $\Lambda_m$ both increase
$\kappa$ decreases, $\Lambda_m$ increases
$\kappa$ increases, $\Lambda_m$ decreases
both decrease
model_answer: **(b).** Fewer ions per unit volume, so $\kappa$ falls; ions from one mole are freer (or more of them, for weak electrolytes), so $\Lambda_m$ rises.

label: PYQ-style
stem: Define molar conductivity. With a sketch, show how it varies with $\sqrt c$ for a strong and a weak electrolyte.
model_answer:
**Molar conductivity** is the conductivity of a solution divided by its molar concentration, $\Lambda_m=\kappa/c$ (S cm$^2$mol$^{-1}$): the conducting power of all ions from one mole of electrolyte. [½]
Strong: small, linear rise on dilution, $\Lambda_m=\Lambda_m^\circ-A\sqrt c$ (ions move more freely). Weak: steep rise at low concentration because the degree of dissociation increases. [1 + ½ graph]

scheme.step: **Molar conductivity** is the conductivity of a solution divided by its molar concentration, $\Lambda_m=\kappa/c$ (S cm$^2$mol$^{-1}$): the conducting power of all ions from one mole of electrolyte.
Strong: small, linear rise on dilution, $\Lambda_m=\Lambda_m^\circ-A\sqrt c$ (ions move more freely). Weak: steep rise at low concentration because the degree of dissociation increases.

hint: Conductivity divided by concentration. Strong: straight line; weak: steep curve near zero.

label: PYQ-style
stem: Write the anode, cathode and overall reactions of the lead storage battery during discharge. What happens to the density of the electrolyte?
model_answer:
Anode: $\ce{Pb(s) + SO4^2-(aq) -> PbSO4(s) + 2e-}$ [½]
Cathode: $\ce{PbO2(s) + SO4^2-(aq) + 4H+(aq) + 2e- -> PbSO4(s) + 2H2O(l)}$ [½]
Overall: $\ce{Pb + PbO2 + 2H2SO4 -> 2PbSO4 + 2H2O}$ [½]
Density **decreases**: H$_2$SO$_4$ is used up and water is formed. [½]

scheme.step: Density **decreases**: H$_2$SO$_4$ is used up and water is formed.

hint: Lead is oxidised and lead dioxide is reduced; both end up as the same solid.

label: PYQ-style
stem:
Calculate the emf at 298 K of the cell
$\ce{Sn(s) | Sn^2+(0.004 M) || H+(0.020 M) | H2(g, 1 bar) | Pt(s)}$
Given $E^\circ_{\ce{Sn^2+/Sn}}=-0.14$ V.
model_answer:
Cell reaction: $\ce{Sn(s) + 2H+(aq) -> Sn^2+(aq) + H2(g)}$, $n=2$ [½]
$E^\circ_\text{cell}=E^\circ_\text{cathode}-E^\circ_\text{anode}=0.00-(-0.14)=0.14$ V [½]
$E_\text{cell}=E^\circ_\text{cell}-\dfrac{0.059}{2}\log\dfrac{[\ce{Sn^2+}]\,p_{\ce{H2}}}{[\ce{H+}]^2}$ [1]
$=0.14-0.0295\log\dfrac{0.004}{(0.020)^2}=0.14-0.0295\log10=\boxed{0.11\text{ V}}$ [1]
hint: Write the cell reaction first. Q = [Sn²⁺]/[H⁺]² and n = 2.

label: PYQ-style
stem: A conductivity cell filled with 0.1 M KCl has resistance 100 $\Omega$. Filled with 0.02 M KCl it has resistance 520 $\Omega$. The conductivity of 0.1 M KCl is 1.29 S m$^{-1}$. Calculate the conductivity and molar conductivity of 0.02 M KCl.
model_answer:
Cell constant $G^*=\kappa R=1.29$ S m$^{-1}\times100\ \Omega=129$ m$^{-1}$ [1]
$\kappa_{0.02\text{ M}}=\dfrac{G^*}{R}=\dfrac{129}{520}=0.248$ S m$^{-1}$ $=\boxed{2.48\times10^{-3}\text{ S cm}^{-1}}$ [1]
$\Lambda_m=\dfrac{1000\,\kappa}{M}=\dfrac{1000\times2.48\times10^{-3}}{0.02}=\boxed{124\text{ S cm}^2\text{mol}^{-1}}$ [1]

scheme.step: Cell constant $G^*=\kappa R=1.29$ S m$^{-1}\times100\ \Omega=129$ m$^{-1}$

hint: Get the cell constant from the 0.1 M data: G* = κ × R. Convert S m⁻¹ to S cm⁻¹.

label: PYQ-style
stem: (a) State Kohlrausch's law. (b) $\Lambda^\circ_m$ for NaCl, HCl and CH$_3$COONa are 126.4, 425.9 and 91.0 S cm$^2$mol$^{-1}$. Find $\Lambda^\circ_m$ of CH$_3$COOH. (c) Why can't this value be found by extrapolating a graph?
model_answer:
(a) **Kohlrausch's law:** the limiting molar conductivity of an electrolyte is the sum of the individual contributions of its cation and anion, $\Lambda_m^\circ=\nu_+\lambda_+^\circ+\nu_-\lambda_-^\circ$. [1]
(b) $\Lambda^\circ_{\ce{CH3COOH}}=\Lambda^\circ_{\ce{CH3COONa}}+\Lambda^\circ_{\ce{HCl}}-\Lambda^\circ_{\ce{NaCl}}=91.0+425.9-126.4=\boxed{390.5\text{ S cm}^2\text{mol}^{-1}}$ [1]
(c) For a weak electrolyte $\Lambda_m$ rises very steeply at low concentration (dissociation keeps increasing), so the curve cannot be extended to zero concentration. [1]

scheme.step: (a) **Kohlrausch's law:** the limiting molar conductivity of an electrolyte is the sum of the individual contributions of its cation and anion, $\Lambda_m^\circ=\nu_+\lambda_+^\circ+\nu_-\lambda_-^\circ$.
(c) For a weak electrolyte $\Lambda_m$ rises very steeply at low concentration (dissociation keeps increasing), so the curve cannot be extended to zero concentration.

hint: Add and subtract the salts so that the unwanted ions cancel.

label: PYQ-style
stem:
(a) For $\ce{2Fe^3+(aq) + 2I-(aq) -> 2Fe^2+(aq) + I2(s)}$, $E^\circ_\text{cell}=0.236$ V at 298 K. Calculate $\Delta_rG^\circ$ and the equilibrium constant. (F = 96500 C mol$^{-1}$) [3]
(b) How many faradays are needed to deposit 1 mol of Al from molten $\ce{Al2O3}$? [1]
(c) Write the electrode reactions of the H$_2$–O$_2$ fuel cell. [1]
model_answer:
(a) $n=2$. $\Delta_rG^\circ=-nFE^\circ_\text{cell}$ [½] $=-2\times96500\times0.236=-45548$ J mol$^{-1}$ $=\boxed{-45.55\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}}$ [1]
$\log K_c=\dfrac{nE^\circ_\text{cell}}{0.059}$ [½] $=\dfrac{2\times0.236}{0.059}=8.0$ ⇒ $K_c=\boxed{1\times10^{8}}$ [1]
(b) $\ce{Al^3+ + 3e- -> Al}$: **3 F** per mole of Al. [1]
(c) Cathode: $\ce{O2(g) + 2H2O(l) + 4e- -> 4OH-(aq)}$ [½]
Anode: $\ce{2H2(g) + 4OH-(aq) -> 4H2O(l) + 4e-}$ [½]

scheme.step: (b) $\ce{Al^3+ + 3e- -> Al}$: **3 F** per mole of Al.

hint: ΔG° = −nFE° with n = 2; then log K = nE°/0.059.

label: PYQ-style
stem: The unit of the cell constant of a conductivity cell is
options: $\Omega$ cm
model_answer: **(b) cm$^{-1}$.** $G^*=l/A$, a length divided by an area.

label: PYQ-style
stem: The function of the salt bridge in a galvanic cell is to
options: supply the electrons that flow in the outer circuit
complete the circuit and keep the two solutions electrically neutral
increase the emf of the cell
stop the cell reaction when the cell is not in use
model_answer: **(b).** Its ions move into the two half-cells to balance the charge that builds up; electrons travel only through the wire.

label: PYQ-style
stem:
**Assertion (A):** The molar conductivity of ethanoic acid rises steeply on dilution.
**Reason (R):** The degree of dissociation of a weak electrolyte increases on dilution.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
model_answer: **(a).** More molecules ionise as the solution is diluted, so one mole of the acid supplies many more ions.
source_note: Added Nov 2026 (objective top-up for live quiz)

label: PYQ-style
stem:
**Assertion (A):** Copper sulphate solution cannot be stored in a zinc vessel.
**Reason (R):** Zinc has a higher standard reduction potential than copper.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
model_answer: **(c).** A is true: zinc displaces copper, $\ce{Zn + Cu^2+ -> Zn^2+ + Cu}$. R is false: $E^\circ$ of $\ce{Zn^2+/Zn}$ ($-0.76$ V) is *lower* than that of $\ce{Cu^2+/Cu}$ (+0.34 V).
source_note: Added Nov 2026 (objective top-up for live quiz)

label: PYQ-style
stem: *An iron bridge near the sea needs repainting far more often than one inland. Rusting is not a simple reaction of iron with air: tiny electrochemical cells form on the wet metal surface. At one spot iron atoms give up electrons; these travel through the metal to another spot, where oxygen dissolved in the water film takes them up. Engineers slow the damage by coating the steel with zinc or by bolting blocks of magnesium to it.*

parts.stem: Write the reaction taking place at the anodic spot.
Why does iron rust faster near the sea?
parts.model_answer: Dissolved salts make the water film a better conductor (an electrolyte), so the electrochemical reactions go faster. [1]

scheme.step: Dissolved salts make the water film a better conductor (an electrolyte), so the electrochemical reactions go faster.

parts.stem: Explain how a zinc coating protects iron even when it is scratched. What is the method of protection with magnesium blocks called?
parts.model_answer: Zinc has a lower reduction potential than iron, so zinc is oxidised in preference and iron stays as the cathode. [1] Sacrificial protection (cathodic protection with a sacrificial anode). [1]

scheme.step: Zinc has a lower reduction potential than iron, so zinc is oxidised in preference and iron stays as the cathode.
Sacrificial protection (cathodic protection with a sacrificial anode).

hint: Treat a rusting spot as a small galvanic cell: decide which metal is oxidised by comparing reduction potentials.
source_note: Added Nov 2026 (from the old case-based angles)
